1	# Quality gates
2	
3	## Anti-rationalization
4	
5	These are excuses agents (and humans) reach for when they want to skip a gate. Each pairs with the reality that makes the excuse wrong. Read this section before relaxing any rule below.
6	
7	| Rationalization | Reality |
8	|---|---|
9	| "This is too small for the spec / phase model" | The phase model is what makes 'small' verifiable. Skipping produces work that cannot be approved. |
10	| "I'll add the phase-approval artifact later" | Without it, the next agent has no audit trail and the loop cannot advance. The artifact *is* the gate. |
11	| "I can just quickly implement this" | Audit-first exists because existing code may already satisfy the goal. Re-implementing without auditing produces drift. |
12	| "The test isn't strictly necessary here" | The testing gate requires a test that would fail if the change were reverted. If you can't write one, you don't understand the change. |
13	| "Two near-duplicates is fine for now" | The DRY gate targets logic that encodes the same invariant in two places. That kind of duplication silently rots when one side changes. |
14	| "I'll skip the planner — the design is obvious" | The planning gate exists for changes that cross layers, touch persistence/auth, or have multiple plausible strategies. 'Obvious' is what missed-the-tradeoff sounds like before review. |
15	| "I'll loosen project settings just for this run" | Project settings are shared. Permissive execution belongs in `settings.local.json` or CLI flags, never committed. |
16	| "Code review can wait until after merge" | The review gate catches duplication, missed drift, and architecture violations the implementer is least likely to see. After-merge review is a documentation step, not a gate. |
17	| "I'll push anyway, CI will catch it" | CI is shared infrastructure. Broken master pages humans, blocks deploys, and disrupts other consumers of the loop. The pre-commit verify gate exists so easy classes of failure are caught locally. |
18	| "I'll skip the verification sprint — nothing changed there" | Cumulative regressions are the failure mode the sprint exists to catch. 'Nothing changed' is an assumption, not evidence. |
19	| "Discovered work can wait for a later phase" | Discovered work that blocks the current phase is part of the current phase. Deferring it produces phases that pass review but don't actually deliver. |
20	
21	If you find yourself making one of these arguments, stop and re-read the relevant gate below.
22	
23	## Universal gate
24	A phase is only complete when all of the following are true:
25	- documented acceptance criteria pass
26	- relevant tests pass
27	- `code-reviewer` approves
28	- `qa-playwright` approves for user-visible or browser-based work
29	- docs are updated for any rule or architecture decision
30	- `artifacts/phase-approval.json` is written with `approved: true`
31	- the outer orchestration layer creates a git commit before the next phase begins
32	
33	## Testing gate
34	A phase is not complete unless:
35	- every new module, endpoint, or public behavior has at least one test exercising its primary path
36	- every bug fix includes a regression test that would fail without the fix
37	- tests are written before or alongside implementation code, not retrofitted after
38	- test names describe the behavior under test, not implementation details
39	- edge cases and error paths are tested for any logic identified as risky in the spec or decision memo
40	
41	When coverage tooling is available in the target project, aim for meaningful branch coverage of new code. Do not pursue a numeric target at the expense of test quality — a focused test that catches real regressions is worth more than broad shallow coverage.
42	
43	"Relevant tests pass" (from the universal gate) means: tests exist that would fail if the feature were removed or the bug fix reverted.
44	
45	### Browser-API limitations (Phase 2b)
46	
47	Some browser APIs (notably `RTCPeerConnection` / WebRTC DataChannel, `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia`, and `DeviceMotionEvent`) cannot be exercised reliably under jsdom or headless Playwright in this project's test environment. Phase 2b's transport handshake and motion-sensor logic are split accordingly:
48	
49	- **Pure-logic modules** (peer state machine, wire format, motion impulse detection, calibration math) remain fully unit-tested under vitest with stubbed browser APIs. These tests gate the testing-gate's "would fail if reverted" rule.
50	- **Transport handshake and live sensor input** are gated by a per-sub-phase manual real-device QA script (`app/verify-phase-2b{1,2,3,4}.mjs`) — same pattern as the existing `verify-phase{4,5}.mjs` flows.
51	- Each Phase 2b sub-phase approval artifact must include a `manual_qa` field naming the device used and the steps performed; without it, the phase is not approved.
52	
53	This is a scoped concession, not a general gate relaxation. See `artifacts/decision-memo.md` §B2 for the full reasoning.
54	
55	## DRY and reuse gate
56	- business rules and validation logic must exist in exactly one place
57	- if the same logic appears in more than one layer, extract it to a shared module or justify the duplication in a decision memo
58	- builders must check for existing utilities and shared modules before creating new ones
59	- code-reviewer must reject changes that introduce unjustified duplication
60	
61	## Drift detection gate
62	Before starting a new implementation phase, the assigned builder must:
63	- review code produced in prior phases for overlap with the current task
64	- flag any inconsistency between the current plan and already-approved code
65	- prefer extending existing modules over creating parallel implementations
66	- report discovered drift as a blocking issue for project-lead to resolve before proceeding
67	
68	## Verification sprint gate
69	Before starting a phase that builds on a completed user-visible or end-to-end foundation, run a full verification of the cumulative system to confirm prior work still functions:
70	- run the complete test suite (unit, integration, and browser/E2E when applicable)
71	- exercise the primary user workflow end-to-end via `qa-playwright` for browser projects, or via the project's domain-equivalent QA (CLI smoke test, integration harness) for non-browser projects
72	- fix any regressions before starting new work — do not layer new complexity onto broken foundations
73	- record verification results under a `verification_sprint` field in the next `artifacts/phase-approval.json`
74	
75	## Planning gate
76	Use a planning and adversarial review cycle before implementation when any of the following are true:
77	- the change crosses multiple layers
78	- persistence or schema choices are involved
79	- auth, security, or public internet exposure is involved
80	- the refactor could invalidate prior assumptions
81	- there are at least two plausible implementation strategies
82	- scaffold control flow, capability generation, or packaging behavior is affected (self-improvement mode)
83	
84	Required outputs:
85	- `artifacts/decision-memo.md`
86	- optional ADR in `docs/adr/` (use `docs/ADR_TEMPLATE.md`; follow naming convention `ADR-NNNN-short-title.md`)
87	
88	## Meta-project gates
89	For scaffold self-improvement work, a phase is not complete until:
90	- the current meta-phase acceptance criteria pass
91	- `strategy-planner` is used for material design changes
92	- `architecture-red-team` is used for architectural or autonomy-affecting changes
93	- `code-reviewer` approves
94	- generated skills validate and package successfully for any skill-related phase
95	- docs and manifest entries are updated
96	- `artifacts/phase-approval.json` is written
97	- the outer wrapper commits the approved phase before the next one begins
98	
99	## Control-loop change gate
100	Any change affecting:
101	- project-lead behavior
102	- quality gates
103	- commit flow
104	- hooks
105	- settings
106	- generation scripts
107	- skill packaging flow
108	- subagent definitions (`.claude/agents/`)
109	
110	must include:
111	- rationale
112	- tradeoffs
113	- rollback path
114	- updated docs
115	- explicit reviewer approval
116	
117	## Commit gate
118	Claude must stop after writing `artifacts/phase-approval.json`.
119	The host-side wrapper is responsible for:
120	1. reading the approval artifact
121	2. running the pre-commit verification gate (see below)
122	3. creating a git commit
123	4. resuming Claude for the next phase
124	
125	## Pre-commit verification gate
126	The wrapper runs a project-defined fast-check command before creating any phase commit, regardless of whether `AUTO_PUSH` is enabled. Mechanism lives in the scaffold (`scripts/run-until-done.sh`); policy lives in the project (`scripts/phasekit-verify.sh`).
127	
128	Scope of the verify command:
129	- fast checks only — lint, typecheck, formatter, unit tests
130	- **not** full E2E or integration suites (those belong to the verification-sprint gate, which Claude drives at phase boundaries)
131	- target under ~30 seconds; this runs every iteration
132	
133	On failure:
134	- the commit is **not** created
135	- the wrapper writes `artifacts/phase-verify-failed.json` with the failing command, exit code, attempt counter, and a tail of the output
136	- the next iteration's `CONTINUE_PROMPT.txt` directs Claude to fix the failure before doing any new phase work
137	- after `VERIFY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (default 3) consecutive failures on the same artifact, the wrapper writes `artifacts/phase-blocked.json` and exits so a human can intervene
138	
139	To recover from a circuit-break: fix the underlying failure (or set `VERIFY_SKIP=1` if the next iteration legitimately needs to commit red), then re-run `scripts/run-until-done.sh`. The wrapper resets the verify-attempt counter at the start of any fresh `CLAUDE_MODE=new` run; `phase-blocked.json` is cleared automatically by the iteration's `cleanup_artifacts` step.
140	
141	Escape hatches:
142	- `VERIFY_SKIP=1` bypasses the gate for one iteration (use sparingly — docs-only phases or TDD phases that intentionally commit a red test)
143	- `PHASEKIT_VERIFY_CMD="..."` overrides the script with a one-shot command
144	
145	Configuration is project-owned: edit `scripts/phasekit-verify.sh` (rendered into the project at enrich time) to declare the right fast checks for the stack. Until configured, the gate fail-opens with a warning so un-instrumented projects continue to work.
146	
147	## Suggested phase approval artifact
148	
149	```json
150	{
151	  "phase": "phase-4",
152	  "approved": true,
153	  "summary": "Primary browser workflow verified and accepted.",
154	  "suggested_commit_message": "phase-4: approve browser workflow"
155	}
156	```
157	
158	For phases that required a planning gate, include a `decision_memo` field referencing the governing artifact:
159	
160	```json
161	{
162	  "phase": "meta-M5.1",
163	  "approved": true,
164	  "summary": "...",
165	  "decision_memo": "artifacts/decision-memo.md",
166	  "suggested_commit_message": "meta-M5.1: ..."
167	}
168	```
169	
170	This field is optional for phases that did not require a planning gate, and required for those that did.
171	
172	## Final completion artifact
173	
174	```json
175	{
176	  "done": true,
177	  "summary": "Required phases completed and production requirements satisfied.",
178	  "final_notes": [
179	    "Known limitation 1",
180	    "Known limitation 2"
181	  ]
182	}
183	```
184	
185	## Discovered work and phase expansion
186	
187	During execution, the lead may discover that the current phase is underspecified or that additional prerequisite work is required.
188	
189	In that case:
190	
191	### Minor discovered work
192	If the new work is small, backward-compatible, and does not require external input:
193	- update the relevant docs directly
194	- append or refine acceptance criteria
195	- continue the current phase without asking the user
196	
197	### Major but self-resolvable discovered work
198	If the new work is substantial but can be resolved using existing repo context and subagents:
199	- invoke strategy-planner and architecture-red-team as needed
200	- update META_SPEC.md, META_PHASES.md, ADRs, or related docs
201	- split the phase into subphases or append follow-on phases as needed
202	- do not ask the user for confirmation merely to continue planning
203	- write `artifacts/phase-update.json` if the phase plan changed materially
204	
205	### External blocker
206	If required information is genuinely missing from the repo and cannot be resolved autonomously:
207	- write `artifacts/phase-blocked.json`
208	- stop without writing `artifacts/phase-approval.json`
209	
210	Approved phase numbering must remain stable. Do not renumber already-approved phases retroactively.

1	# PointFight Reactor
2	
3	## Purpose
4	PointFight Reactor is a local-first browser application for sport karate / point
5	fighting reaction training. It helps the athlete rebuild fast decision commitment
6	by presenting randomized visuospatial cues, opponent video clips, go/no-go
7	situations, and measurable reaction drills — coupled to a real physical response.
8	
9	The app is designed for solo training in a home gym using a laptop or large
10	screen, pads, a foot pedal or phone-as-sensor for physical input, and an
11	optional webcam.
12	
13	## Primary User
14	A high-level point fighter preparing for competition in 2 weeks. The athlete is
15	already fit and technically skilled. The problem is not conditioning; the
16	problem is hesitation, over-analysis, and delayed commitment under visual
17	uncertainty.
18	
19	## Core Training Principle
20	The app trains perception-action coupling:
21	
22	- See a specific opponent trigger.
23	- Commit instantly to a preselected physical response.
24	- Reset, keep moving.
25	- Measure correctness, reaction time, and hesitation.
26	
27	The app should discourage half-commitments. In scoring, hesitation is worse
28	than a clean wrong decision. Reps must require a physical commitment, not a
29	keyboard tap from a seated position — keyboard input is supported only as a
30	fallback for setup and development.
31	
32	## Training Goals This App Supports
33	- **Decision-making** under visual uncertainty (go/no-go discrimination).
34	- **Reaction speed** measured from a visual cue to a real motor commitment.
35	- **Distance management** as a second decision axis (cue + range → response).
36	- **Workout load**: reps live inside timed rounds with continuous movement
37	  between cues, not seated reaction-time testing.
38	
39	## MVP Features
40	1. Fullscreen drill mode.
41	2. Randomized cue presentation with visuospatial (not text-only) cues.
42	3. Configurable pre-cue delay range with continuous-motion expectation.
43	4. Go/no-go cue logic with optional distance modifier.
44	5. Physical response input: foot pedal (USB HID), phone-as-sensor
45	   (accelerometer threshold), or keyboard fallback.
46	6. Reaction-time measurement with choice-RT thresholds (not simple-RT).
47	7. Correct / late / false-start / hesitation scoring with operationalized
48	   hesitation definition.
49	8. Round-based session structure (configurable round length and rest).
50	9. Session history saved locally.
51	10. CSV/JSON export.
52	11. Simple drill configuration screen.
53	
54	## Cue Representation
55	Cues are presented as animated silhouettes or symbols, not English text.
56	Text labels are available as a learning/debug overlay only.
57	
58	Each cue has:
59	- a visual form (SVG animation or symbol)
60	- a cue type
61	- an optional distance attribute (far / mid / in-range)
62	- a go/no-go classification (which may depend on distance)
63	
64	## Cue Types
65	- opponent steps in
66	- opponent blitzes
67	- opponent lifts lead leg
68	- opponent drops lead hand
69	- opponent retreats
70	- opponent freezes
71	- opponent fake-steps
72	- no-go bait
73	
74	## Response Types
75	- blitz
76	- stop-kick
77	- angle counter
78	- jam entry
79	- evade/reset
80	- do nothing
81	
82	## Distance Axis
83	Each go cue may carry a distance attribute that changes the correct response:
84	- **Far**: most cues are no-go; pressure or reset only.
85	- **Mid**: blitz / jam window; the primary commit zone.
86	- **In-range**: stop-kick, jam entry, or evade — never a clean blitz.
87	
88	Distance is rendered visually via silhouette size and optionally via a
89	continuous audio tone whose pitch tracks range.
90	
91	## Drill Types
92	
93	### First Beat
94	A cue appears. Athlete must respond immediately with one committed scoring
95	action.
96	
97	### Go / No-Go
98	Some cues are valid openings. Others are baits. Athlete responds only to
99	valid triggers.
100	
101	### Counter Entry
102	Athlete reacts to incoming attacks with a preselected counter.
103	
104	### Rhythm Break
105	Athlete attacks when the opponent's movement rhythm changes.
106	
107	### Tournament Start
108	Simulates bow/start/first exchange/reset.
109	
110	### Round Workout
111	Drill runs inside fixed-length rounds (default 2:00 work / 1:00 rest, configurable)
112	with continuous movement expected between cues. Optional penalty counter
113	(e.g. burpees added to a rest-period clear-list) for false starts and
114	hesitations.
115	
116	## Scoring
117	Each rep records:
118	- cue id
119	- cue type
120	- distance (if applicable)
121	- expected response
122	- athlete response (input source: pedal / phone / keyboard)
123	- reaction time (ms)
124	- correct / incorrect
125	- false start (input before cue)
126	- late response (input after the choice-RT threshold)
127	- hesitation (input within window but above the hesitation threshold)
128	
129	Operational definitions:
130	- **Late** = response after `late_threshold_ms` (default 600 ms).
131	- **Hesitation** = response between `hesitation_threshold_ms` (default
132	  450 ms) and `late_threshold_ms`, on a go cue.
133	- **False start** = input received during the pre-cue delay window.
134	
135	Suggested scoring:
136	- correct go: +1
137	- correct no-go: +1
138	- late go: 0
139	- false start: -1
140	- hesitation / half-go: -2
141	
142	## Session Summary
143	Beyond aggregate stats, the summary breaks down:
144	- RT mean / median / best-10-avg per cue type
145	- error rate per cue type
146	- false-start position in sequence (detect rhythm-anticipation patterns)
147	- no-go discrimination accuracy
148	- distance-axis accuracy (if enabled)
149	
150	## Non-Goals for MVP
151	- Multiplayer
152	- Cloud account system
153	- AI-generated video
154	- Perfect pose detection
155	- Mobile-first design (phone is sensor only, not primary UI)
156	
157	## Future Features
158	- Local video clip tagging
159	- Webcam-based movement detection
160	- Opponent pose analysis
161	- Personalized drill recommendations (e.g. auto-weighting cues you fail on)
162	- Tournament taper mode

29	### B1 — Pairing trust model
30	
31	The earlier draft proposed an offer-SDP nonce. It is removed.
32	
33	Phase 2b's threat model is *home-gym Wi-Fi*: a single athlete trains alone,
34	the LAN is trusted, and the worst plausible attack is a roommate connecting
35	their phone for amusement. We do not build cryptographic peer auth for that.
36	Pairing is implicitly authorized by the human physically holding the phone
37	that scanned the QR (2b.2) or pasted the offer (2b.1).
38	
39	**Concretely**: 2b.1 accepts any answer whose SDP parses cleanly. Future
40	versions, if a real threat model emerges, can wrap the SDP in a signed
41	envelope. Do not ship vague "light auth" claims.
42	
43	### B2 — WebRTC test-gate concession
44	
45	Per `docs/QUALITY_GATES.md` *Testing gate*: every public behavior needs a
46	test that would fail when the behavior is reverted. WebRTC handshakes and
47	`getUserMedia` cannot be exercised reliably under jsdom or headless
48	Playwright. This memo formally records the following concession:
49	
50	- **Pure logic** (peer-state machine, wire format, motion impulse detection,
51	  calibration math) is fully unit-tested under vitest. These tests gate the
52	  builder's claim that the modules behave correctly.
53	- **Transport handshake and motion events** are gated by a documented
54	  manual-QA script (`app/verify-phase-2b1.mjs` etc.) modeled on the existing
55	  `app/verify-phase4.mjs` / `app/verify-phase5.mjs` pattern. Each sub-phase
56	  ships a verify script and a checklist signed off in
57	  `artifacts/phase-2bN-verify/results.json`.
58	- **The phase-approval artifact for each sub-phase must include a
59	  `manual_qa` field** listing the steps performed and the device used.
60	  Without that field, the phase is not approved.
61	
62	This is a project-specific deviation from the universal testing gate. It is
63	limited in scope to Phase 2b transport/sensor work and is justified by the
64	unavailability of WebRTC + DeviceMotion in the project's automated test
65	environment. Document this in `docs/QUALITY_GATES.md` (a one-line
66	"Browser-API limitations" footnote — not a gate rewrite) as part of 2b.1.
67	
68	### B3 — Falsifiable 2b.3 acceptance
69	
70	The "within 50ms of the impulse peak" criterion is unobservable from the
71	laptop. Rewritten 2b.3 acceptance criteria:
72	
73	- 60s at rest on a flat surface → **0** commit events received by the laptop.
74	- 5 deliberate forward-snap impulses (single user, single session) → **5**
75	  commit events received (±0).
76	- Double-snap within the debounce window (300ms) → **1** commit event.
77	- Calibration: 5 sample swings → threshold persists; re-running calibration
78	  overwrites the prior threshold; threshold survives page reload.
79	
80	All four are observable from the laptop's debug surface (2b.1 already ships
81	the receive-side timestamp display) and falsifiable on a real device.

83	### B4 — Phone OS strategy: ship for both, gate on Android
84	
85	`docs/SPEC.md` does not specify the athlete's phone OS. The previous draft
86	hedged. Final strategy:
87	
88	- **2b.1, 2b.2, 2b.3 acceptance is gated on Android** (Chrome over plain
89	  HTTP on LAN). The athlete can install the companion page on Android in
90	  about 10 seconds with no certificate dance.
91	- **iOS support is shipped as a documented path** in `docs/SETUP_IOS.md`
92	  (authored in 2b.3): install mkcert on the laptop, generate a LAN cert,
93	  install the root CA on the iPhone, serve Vite with `--https`. iOS
94	  motion permission then works.
95	- **If the athlete is on iOS**, they follow `docs/SETUP_IOS.md` *once*. The
96	  failure mode (cert dance is too painful) is recoverable: the athlete
97	  falls back to pedal + keyboard, which already covers the
98	  "physical commitment" requirement per the existing PHASES.md rationale
99	  for Phase 2b's deprioritization.
100	- **If the athlete is on Android**, no extra setup. The companion page works.
101	
102	This avoids blocking on a question the project's source-of-truth docs
103	cannot answer (SPEC.md is silent) while ensuring no user is left without a
104	path. The acceptance gate is Android; iOS is documented but not CI-gated.

### Red-team review — Phase 6 decomposition

1. **Hidden coupling / drift risk (forked rep-commit path).** **MODIFY.**
   §3 says "`useSession` is **not** reused for clip mode — clip runner
   produces its own `RepRecord`s and `SessionRecord` directly via the
   existing `saveRep` / `saveSession` helpers." Then §7/R3 admits "Could
   drift. Mitigation considered: extract a `commitRep()` helper to a
   new `engine/persistence.ts`. Decided **against** for Phase 6.1–6.3."
   This contradicts the DRY gate (`docs/QUALITY_GATES.md` §"DRY and
   reuse gate": "if the same logic appears in more than one layer,
   extract it to a shared module or justify the duplication in a
   decision memo"). The bypass duplicates the invariants encoded in
   `commitRep()` in `src/store/session.ts` lines 107–139: rep-id
   minting, `resolveCueAtDistance`, the `roundIndex` + `inputSource`
   fan-out, the `persistSession(null)` call after each rep, and the
   `feedback` state hand-off. That is at least five invariants Phase-5
   analytics already depend on, not "~30 lines of boilerplate." Any
   future change to `RepRecord` shape (e.g., adding a `responseId`
   field, or wiring the distance axis into clip mode) has to be made
   in two places or it silently rots. **Required change:** extract a
   pure `commitRep(input) -> { rep, summary }` helper in
   `engine/persistence.ts` (or `engine/rep.ts`) in 6.3 itself, not as a
   future refactor. `session.ts` and `clipmode/runner.ts` both call it.
   The "~30 LOC" argument is not a justification — it is the exact
   shape of duplication the DRY gate names. Either justify in writing
   why the two call sites encode *different* invariants (they don't —
   §4 explicitly says `classifyRep()` is reused as-is, so the invariant
   *is* the same), or extract.

2. **Schema evolution safety (Dexie v4).** **MODIFY.** The memo at §1
   says "Bump `db.ts` to `version(4)`" and at §5 says "bump to
   `version(4)`, add `clips: 'id, importedAt'`, add `clipId` to the
   `reps` index → `reps: 'id, sessionId, cueId, clipId'`." Two
   problems. (a) Adding an *index* to an existing Dexie store is a
   schema change Dexie handles by re-indexing, but the memo does not
   specify whether the `version(4).stores(...)` block must include
   *all four* tables (sessions, reps, settings, profiles, clips) — the
   existing pattern at `src/store/db.ts:14-28` redeclares every table
   in each version. Omitting any table in v4 drops it. **Required
   change:** the 6.1 acceptance criteria must explicitly state the
   full v4 `.stores()` declaration: `sessions: 'id, startedAt', reps:
   'id, sessionId, cueId, clipId', settings: 'id', profiles: 'id,
   createdAt', clips: 'id, importedAt'`. (b) The memo asserts existing
   v3 records remain valid because `clipId` and `mode` are *optional*.
   True for the data shape, but Dexie does not migrate or rewrite
   existing rows; the new `clipId` index will simply be `undefined` on
   old reps and they will not appear in `where('clipId').equals(id)`
   queries. The memo should state this explicitly so reviewers don't
   assume migration. **Required change:** add a "schema migration
   notes" sub-bullet under 6.1 acceptance: "v3 reps remain readable; no
   data migration; `where('clipId').equals(...)` on old reps returns
   empty (intended)."

3. **Acceptance-criteria falsifiability.** **MODIFY.** Several 6.1–6.3
   criteria are not falsifiable in an automated test:
   - 6.1 "Reload preserves the list" — testable via Dexie.
   - 6.1 "Quota estimate visible; warning at >80 %" — testable by
     stubbing `navigator.storage.estimate()`.
   - 6.2 "Scrub + frame-step land within 1 frame of the chosen
     position" — **not testable without a real `<video>` element**;
     jsdom does not implement `HTMLMediaElement.play()` /
     `currentTime` write semantics. This is the same class of
     concession as Phase 2b §B2 (WebRTC + DeviceMotion). The memo
     does not call this out.
   - 6.3 "Cue-shown event lands within ±33 ms of tagged frame
     (verified by `requestVideoFrameCallback` callback timestamp)"
     — same: `requestVideoFrameCallback` is not in jsdom. Manual-QA
     only.
   - 6.3 "drill plays clips in random order" — see concern 7 below;
     "random order" is not falsifiable without a distribution spec.

   **Required change:** add a §B5 cross-cut (or §6.0 sub-section)
   titled "Browser-API limitations — Phase 6" that names HTML5
   `<video>`, `requestVideoFrameCallback`, and `navigator.storage`
   as untestable in jsdom, lists which acceptance criteria are
   manual-QA-gated (6.2 scrub precision; 6.3 cue-shown timing), and
   requires `app/verify-phase-6{1,2,3}.mjs` scripts plus a `manual_qa`
   field in each sub-phase approval — mirroring the Phase 2b
   `docs/QUALITY_GATES.md` §"Browser-API limitations (Phase 2b)"
   footnote. Without this, 6.2 and 6.3 will be approved with no
   "would-fail-if-reverted" test for their core RT behavior.

4. **Storage quota / failure modes.** **MODIFY.** §1 says "Mitigation
   for quota exhaustion: surface `navigator.storage.estimate()` in the
   clip-library screen, warn at >80 % usage, hard-cap at >95 % with
   'delete a clip first'. No silent failures." This is good in
   principle but the 6.1 acceptance criteria do not test the
   *failure* path. What happens when `addClip(blob)` is called while
   already at 96 %? When Dexie's `put()` rejects with QuotaExceededError
   mid-write? The current code at `src/store/db.ts:61-69` swallows
   errors into `_openError` and returns void — `addClip` will need a
   different shape (return `{ ok: true } | { ok: false, reason }`)
   because the user MUST see the failure. **Required change:** 6.1
   acceptance must include (a) an `addClip` return type that surfaces
   QuotaExceeded as a typed result, not a void/swallowed error;
   (b) a unit test that stubs Dexie to throw `QuotaExceededError`
   and asserts the UI shows a non-silent error; (c) an explicit
   per-clip size cap (recommend 200 MB hard, 100 MB soft warning)
   so a single pathological upload cannot exhaust the budget. The
   memo's "~30 clips × 50 MB ≈ 1.5 GB" math assumes athletes will
   trim clips; nothing enforces it.

5. **RT precision under `requestVideoFrameCallback`.** **MODIFY.**
   §4 says "HTML5 `<video>` `timeupdate` fires at ~250 ms resolution.
   Using `requestVideoFrameCallback` (Chrome 83+, Safari 15.4+) brings
   this to per-frame (~16 ms at 60 fps)." §7/R2 then admits Safari <
   15.4 falls back to 250 ms. With the spec's hesitation threshold at
   450 ms and late threshold at 600 ms (`docs/SPEC.md` "Operational
   definitions"), a 250 ms `timeupdate` quantization means a press
   that classifies as "correct" on Chrome could classify as
   "hesitation" on old Safari — **the same press, the same clip**.
   That is measurement-system incoherence, not a "degraded precision"
   nuisance. R2 says "ship anyway with degraded precision" is on the
   table; that is not acceptable when the spec defines hesitation in
   tens-of-ms terms. **Required change:** pick path (a) from R2 —
   feature-detect `requestVideoFrameCallback` and refuse to enable
   Clip mode when absent. Add a 6.3 acceptance: "On a browser without
   `requestVideoFrameCallback`, IdleScreen's Clip-mode start button
   is disabled with the message 'Clip mode requires Chrome 83+,
   Edge, or Safari 15.4+'." This is the same shape as the existing
   "Phone not paired" gate in `src/ui/IdleScreen.tsx:60-81`.

6. **Mode-selector UX coupling.** **MODIFY.** §6 6.3 says "`IdleScreen`
   gains a 'Clip mode' start button that requires ≥1 tagged clip" and
   §7/R6 punts the UX shape to red-team. The matrix is real:
   inputSource ∈ {keyboard, pedal, phone} × mode ∈ {live, clip} = 6
   combinations. Phone-input + clip-mode is *not* nonsensical — the
   athlete stands in front of the laptop screen and the phone is
   strapped to their hand/foot — that is exactly how Phase 2b.3's
   calibration assumes phone is mounted. So all 6 combos are valid
   in principle. But the current IdleScreen already gates on
   phone-pairing (`src/ui/IdleScreen.tsx:38-40`): `phoneSelected &&
   !phoneReady` disables Start. In clip mode that gate still applies.
   **Required change:** 6.3 must explicitly state "Clip-mode Start
   inherits the existing phone-pairing gate from `IdleScreen`. Clip
   mode does **not** override inputSource; the user's configured
   inputSource is used to record presses." Also pick the UX shape
   *before* 6.3 ships, not as a follow-on: a segmented control above
   the Start button (Live / Clip) is the right answer because adding
   a second "Start" button breaks the existing single-`autoFocus`
   button affordance at `IdleScreen.tsx:94`. Specify this in the
   memo so 6.3 doesn't churn the shell twice.

7. **Random clip selection invariants.** **MODIFY.** §6 6.3
   acceptance says "Start 'Clip mode' with 3 tagged clips → drill
   plays clips in random order." §6 also says "Random selection via
   existing `rng.ts`; weighted-by-untaped-recently is *out of scope*."
   That is not enough to write a failing test. **Required change:** pin
   the distribution explicitly. Recommended: "uniform random with
   replacement, no repeat-immediately-previous constraint" (mirrors
   `pickNextCue` semantics). Then the test can be `for i in 0..200:
   pick; assert each of N clips appears within ±20% of N/200`. Also
   state explicitly that untagged clips are excluded (already implied
   by 6.2's "excluded from playback in 6.3" but worth restating in 6.3
   itself).

8. **Sub-phase ordering.** **ACCEPTED.** 6.1 → 6.2 → 6.3 is correct:
   6.2 needs persisted clips (you cannot tag what you cannot save and
   reload), so an "in-memory clip stash that gets replaced by Dexie
   later" would force re-importing every page reload and would
   actively block athlete dogfooding of tagging UX. The order does
   not lock in throwaway scaffolding — each sub-phase produces real,
   non-disposable surface area.

9. **Cross-cutting concerns from prior phases.** **BLOCK.** The
   memo does not include a §B5 (or equivalent) cross-cut analogous
   to Phase 2b's §B1–B4. Specifically missing: (a) browser-API
   testing concession for `<video>` and `requestVideoFrameCallback`
   (overlaps with concern 3 above — must be written into the memo,
   not just acknowledged in this review); (b) browser-version gate
   for Clip mode (overlaps with concern 5); (c) the equivalent of
   §B3 "falsifiable acceptance" — most of 6.2 and 6.3's acceptance
   criteria as written are *demonstrable* but not *falsifiable in
   CI*. This is a structural omission, not a typo. **Required next
   action:** the planner must append §B5 (browser-API limitations
   for Phase 6) and §B6 (falsifiable acceptance for clip-mode RT
   timing) to the "Resolved red-team blockers" section, mirroring
   the Phase 2b pattern, and update `docs/QUALITY_GATES.md` §
   "Browser-API limitations" to add a Phase-6 entry alongside Phase
   2b. No sub-phase approval should proceed without this.

10. **Project-complete signal.** **MODIFY.** The memo is silent on
    whether shipping Phase 6 (or its sub-phases) triggers the
    `done: true` final-completion artifact (`docs/QUALITY_GATES.md`
    §"Final completion artifact"). `docs/PHASES.md:182` marks Phase 6
    as "post-tournament unless ahead of schedule"; Phase 7 (webcam
    pose) is also "post-tournament." The autonomous loop needs a
    clean stop. **Required change:** add a "Project-complete
    signal" sub-section to the memo stating: "Shipping 6.1+6.2+6.3
    satisfies the Phase 6 acceptance criteria in `docs/PHASES.md`.
    Phase 7 (Webcam Pose Detection) is explicitly marked
    post-tournament and is NOT a project-complete blocker per
    `docs/SPEC.md` §'Non-Goals for MVP' ('Perfect pose detection')
    and §'Future Features' ('Webcam-based movement detection').
    The wrapper should write `artifacts/phase-approval.json` for
    6.3 with a `project_complete: true` flag (or write
    `done: true` directly) so the loop terminates."

**Verdict.** Send back to planner for a tightened revision. The plan
is structurally sound — the storage choice is right, the sub-phase
ordering is right, and §4's "no engine change" insight is the
correct lever. But concern 9 (missing §B5/B6 cross-cuts) is a
**BLOCK**, and the cluster of MODIFY findings (concerns 1, 3, 4, 5,
6, 10) are not "nice to have" — they are the difference between a
phase that can be tested and approved versus one that ships unreviewable
behavior under "manual-QA-only" cover. In particular: concern 1
(the forked rep-commit path) directly violates the DRY gate as
written, and concern 5 (Safari `<` 15.4 measurement incoherence)
would let the app silently report nonsense reaction times. None of
these requires re-architecting; all are concrete edits to the memo +
explicit gates added to the acceptance criteria. After the planner
revises and adds §B5/§B6 and the per-concern fixes above, the plan
is safe to advance to phase-update.

### Red-team review — Phase 6 decomposition

1. **Hidden coupling / drift risk (forked rep-commit path).** **MODIFY.**
   §3 says "`useSession` is **not** reused for clip mode — clip runner
   produces its own `RepRecord`s and `SessionRecord` directly via the
   existing `saveRep` / `saveSession` helpers." Then §7/R3 admits "Could
   drift. Mitigation considered: extract a `commitRep()` helper to a
   new `engine/persistence.ts`. Decided **against** for Phase 6.1–6.3."
   This contradicts the DRY gate (`docs/QUALITY_GATES.md` §"DRY and
   reuse gate": "if the same logic appears in more than one layer,
   extract it to a shared module or justify the duplication in a
   decision memo"). The bypass duplicates the invariants encoded in
   `commitRep()` in `src/store/session.ts` lines 107–139: rep-id
   minting, `resolveCueAtDistance`, the `roundIndex` + `inputSource`
   fan-out, the `persistSession(null)` call after each rep, and the
   `feedback` state hand-off. That is at least five invariants Phase-5
   analytics already depend on, not "~30 lines of boilerplate." Any
   future change to `RepRecord` shape (e.g., adding a `responseId`
   field, or wiring the distance axis into clip mode) has to be made
   in two places or it silently rots. **Required change:** extract a
   pure `commitRep(input) -> { rep, summary }` helper in
   `engine/persistence.ts` (or `engine/rep.ts`) in 6.3 itself, not as a
   future refactor. `session.ts` and `clipmode/runner.ts` both call it.
   The "~30 LOC" argument is not a justification — it is the exact
   shape of duplication the DRY gate names. Either justify in writing
   why the two call sites encode *different* invariants (they don't —
   §4 explicitly says `classifyRep()` is reused as-is, so the invariant
   *is* the same), or extract.

2. **Schema evolution safety (Dexie v4).** **MODIFY.** The memo at §1
   says "Bump `db.ts` to `version(4)`" and at §5 says "bump to
   `version(4)`, add `clips: 'id, importedAt'`, add `clipId` to the
   `reps` index → `reps: 'id, sessionId, cueId, clipId'`." Two
   problems. (a) Adding an *index* to an existing Dexie store is a
   schema change Dexie handles by re-indexing, but the memo does not
   specify whether the `version(4).stores(...)` block must include
   *all four* tables (sessions, reps, settings, profiles, clips) — the
   existing pattern at `src/store/db.ts:14-28` redeclares every table
   in each version. Omitting any table in v4 drops it. **Required
   change:** the 6.1 acceptance criteria must explicitly state the
   full v4 `.stores()` declaration: `sessions: 'id, startedAt', reps:
   'id, sessionId, cueId, clipId', settings: 'id', profiles: 'id,
   createdAt', clips: 'id, importedAt'`. (b) The memo asserts existing
   v3 records remain valid because `clipId` and `mode` are *optional*.
   True for the data shape, but Dexie does not migrate or rewrite
   existing rows; the new `clipId` index will simply be `undefined` on
   old reps and they will not appear in `where('clipId').equals(id)`
   queries. The memo should state this explicitly so reviewers don't
   assume migration. **Required change:** add a "schema migration
   notes" sub-bullet under 6.1 acceptance: "v3 reps remain readable; no
   data migration; `where('clipId').equals(...)` on old reps returns
   empty (intended)."

3. **Acceptance-criteria falsifiability.** **MODIFY.** Several 6.1–6.3
   criteria are not falsifiable in an automated test:
   - 6.1 "Reload preserves the list" — testable via Dexie.
   - 6.1 "Quota estimate visible; warning at >80 %" — testable by
     stubbing `navigator.storage.estimate()`.
   - 6.2 "Scrub + frame-step land within 1 frame of the chosen
     position" — **not testable without a real `<video>` element**;
     jsdom does not implement `HTMLMediaElement.play()` /
     `currentTime` write semantics. This is the same class of
     concession as Phase 2b §B2 (WebRTC + DeviceMotion). The memo
     does not call this out.
   - 6.3 "Cue-shown event lands within ±33 ms of tagged frame
     (verified by `requestVideoFrameCallback` callback timestamp)"
     — same: `requestVideoFrameCallback` is not in jsdom. Manual-QA
     only.
   - 6.3 "drill plays clips in random order" — see concern 7 below;
     "random order" is not falsifiable without a distribution spec.

   **Required change:** add a §B5 cross-cut (or §6.0 sub-section)
   titled "Browser-API limitations — Phase 6" that names HTML5
   `<video>`, `requestVideoFrameCallback`, and `navigator.storage`
   as untestable in jsdom, lists which acceptance criteria are
   manual-QA-gated (6.2 scrub precision; 6.3 cue-shown timing), and
   requires `app/verify-phase-6{1,2,3}.mjs` scripts plus a `manual_qa`
   field in each sub-phase approval — mirroring the Phase 2b
   `docs/QUALITY_GATES.md` §"Browser-API limitations (Phase 2b)"
   footnote. Without this, 6.2 and 6.3 will be approved with no
   "would-fail-if-reverted" test for their core RT behavior.

4. **Storage quota / failure modes.** **MODIFY.** §1 says "Mitigation
   for quota exhaustion: surface `navigator.storage.estimate()` in the
   clip-library screen, warn at >80 % usage, hard-cap at >95 % with
   'delete a clip first'. No silent failures." This is good in
   principle but the 6.1 acceptance criteria do not test the
   *failure* path. What happens when `addClip(blob)` is called while
   already at 96 %? When Dexie's `put()` rejects with QuotaExceededError
   mid-write? The current code at `src/store/db.ts:61-69` swallows
   errors into `_openError` and returns void — `addClip` will need a
   different shape (return `{ ok: true } | { ok: false, reason }`)
   because the user MUST see the failure. **Required change:** 6.1
   acceptance must include (a) an `addClip` return type that surfaces
   QuotaExceeded as a typed result, not a void/swallowed error;
   (b) a unit test that stubs Dexie to throw `QuotaExceededError`
   and asserts the UI shows a non-silent error; (c) an explicit
   per-clip size cap (recommend 200 MB hard, 100 MB soft warning)
   so a single pathological upload cannot exhaust the budget. The
   memo's "~30 clips × 50 MB ≈ 1.5 GB" math assumes athletes will
   trim clips; nothing enforces it.

5. **RT precision under `requestVideoFrameCallback`.** **MODIFY.**
   §4 says "HTML5 `<video>` `timeupdate` fires at ~250 ms resolution.
   Using `requestVideoFrameCallback` (Chrome 83+, Safari 15.4+) brings
   this to per-frame (~16 ms at 60 fps)." §7/R2 then admits Safari <
   15.4 falls back to 250 ms. With the spec's hesitation threshold at
   450 ms and late threshold at 600 ms (`docs/SPEC.md` "Operational
   definitions"), a 250 ms `timeupdate` quantization means a press
   that classifies as "correct" on Chrome could classify as
   "hesitation" on old Safari — **the same press, the same clip**.
   That is measurement-system incoherence, not a "degraded precision"
   nuisance. R2 says "ship anyway with degraded precision" is on the
   table; that is not acceptable when the spec defines hesitation in
   tens-of-ms terms. **Required change:** pick path (a) from R2 —
   feature-detect `requestVideoFrameCallback` and refuse to enable
   Clip mode when absent. Add a 6.3 acceptance: "On a browser without
   `requestVideoFrameCallback`, IdleScreen's Clip-mode start button
   is disabled with the message 'Clip mode requires Chrome 83+,
   Edge, or Safari 15.4+'." This is the same shape as the existing
   "Phone not paired" gate in `src/ui/IdleScreen.tsx:60-81`.

6. **Mode-selector UX coupling.** **MODIFY.** §6 6.3 says "`IdleScreen`
   gains a 'Clip mode' start button that requires ≥1 tagged clip" and
   §7/R6 punts the UX shape to red-team. The matrix is real:
   inputSource ∈ {keyboard, pedal, phone} × mode ∈ {live, clip} = 6
   combinations. Phone-input + clip-mode is *not* nonsensical — the
   athlete stands in front of the laptop screen and the phone is
   strapped to their hand/foot — that is exactly how Phase 2b.3's
   calibration assumes phone is mounted. So all 6 combos are valid
   in principle. But the current IdleScreen already gates on
   phone-pairing (`src/ui/IdleScreen.tsx:38-40`): `phoneSelected &&
   !phoneReady` disables Start. In clip mode that gate still applies.
   **Required change:** 6.3 must explicitly state "Clip-mode Start
   inherits the existing phone-pairing gate from `IdleScreen`. Clip
   mode does **not** override inputSource; the user's configured
   inputSource is used to record presses." Also pick the UX shape
   *before* 6.3 ships, not as a follow-on: a segmented control above
   the Start button (Live / Clip) is the right answer because adding
   a second "Start" button breaks the existing single-`autoFocus`
   button affordance at `IdleScreen.tsx:94`. Specify this in the
   memo so 6.3 doesn't churn the shell twice.

7. **Random clip selection invariants.** **MODIFY.** §6 6.3
   acceptance says "Start 'Clip mode' with 3 tagged clips → drill
   plays clips in random order." §6 also says "Random selection via
   existing `rng.ts`; weighted-by-untaped-recently is *out of scope*."
   That is not enough to write a failing test. **Required change:** pin
   the distribution explicitly. Recommended: "uniform random with
   replacement, no repeat-immediately-previous constraint" (mirrors
   `pickNextCue` semantics). Then the test can be `for i in 0..200:
   pick; assert each of N clips appears within ±20% of N/200`. Also
   state explicitly that untagged clips are excluded (already implied
   by 6.2's "excluded from playback in 6.3" but worth restating in 6.3
   itself).

8. **Sub-phase ordering.** **ACCEPTED.** 6.1 → 6.2 → 6.3 is correct:
   6.2 needs persisted clips (you cannot tag what you cannot save and
   reload), so an "in-memory clip stash that gets replaced by Dexie
   later" would force re-importing every page reload and would
   actively block athlete dogfooding of tagging UX. The order does
   not lock in throwaway scaffolding — each sub-phase produces real,
   non-disposable surface area.

9. **Cross-cutting concerns from prior phases.** **BLOCK.** The
   memo does not include a §B5 (or equivalent) cross-cut analogous
   to Phase 2b's §B1–B4. Specifically missing: (a) browser-API
   testing concession for `<video>` and `requestVideoFrameCallback`
   (overlaps with concern 3 above — must be written into the memo,
   not just acknowledged in this review); (b) browser-version gate
   for Clip mode (overlaps with concern 5); (c) the equivalent of
   §B3 "falsifiable acceptance" — most of 6.2 and 6.3's acceptance
   criteria as written are *demonstrable* but not *falsifiable in
   CI*. This is a structural omission, not a typo. **Required next
   action:** the planner must append §B5 (browser-API limitations
   for Phase 6) and §B6 (falsifiable acceptance for clip-mode RT
   timing) to the "Resolved red-team blockers" section, mirroring
   the Phase 2b pattern, and update `docs/QUALITY_GATES.md` §
   "Browser-API limitations" to add a Phase-6 entry alongside Phase
   2b. No sub-phase approval should proceed without this.

10. **Project-complete signal.** **MODIFY.** The memo is silent on
    whether shipping Phase 6 (or its sub-phases) triggers the
    `done: true` final-completion artifact (`docs/QUALITY_GATES.md`
    §"Final completion artifact"). `docs/PHASES.md:182` marks Phase 6
    as "post-tournament unless ahead of schedule"; Phase 7 (webcam
    pose) is also "post-tournament." The autonomous loop needs a
    clean stop. **Required change:** add a "Project-complete
    signal" sub-section to the memo stating: "Shipping 6.1+6.2+6.3
    satisfies the Phase 6 acceptance criteria in `docs/PHASES.md`.
    Phase 7 (Webcam Pose Detection) is explicitly marked
    post-tournament and is NOT a project-complete blocker per
    `docs/SPEC.md` §'Non-Goals for MVP' ('Perfect pose detection')
    and §'Future Features' ('Webcam-based movement detection').
    The wrapper should write `artifacts/phase-approval.json` for
    6.3 with a `project_complete: true` flag (or write
    `done: true` directly) so the loop terminates."

**Verdict.** Send back to planner for a tightened revision. The plan
is structurally sound — the storage choice is right, the sub-phase
ordering is right, and §4's "no engine change" insight is the
correct lever. But concern 9 (missing §B5/B6 cross-cuts) is a
**BLOCK**, and the cluster of MODIFY findings (concerns 1, 3, 4, 5,
6, 10) are not "nice to have" — they are the difference between a
phase that can be tested and approved versus one that ships unreviewable
behavior under "manual-QA-only" cover. In particular: concern 1
(the forked rep-commit path) directly violates the DRY gate as
written, and concern 5 (Safari `<` 15.4 measurement incoherence)
would let the app silently report nonsense reaction times. None of
these requires re-architecting; all are concrete edits to the memo +
explicit gates added to the acceptance criteria. After the planner
revises and adds §B5/§B6 and the per-concern fixes above, the plan
is safe to advance to phase-update.

709	## Phase 6 decomposition memo — Video Opponent Mode
710	
711	### Decision summary
712	- Clip mode is a **separate input/render path** that reuses the existing
713	  `recordPress(at)` boundary and `RepRecord` schema with one additive
714	  field. No engine surgery.
715	- Clips are stored as **Blob in Dexie** (Option A). Largest realistic
716	  Phase-6 library is ~30 clips × 50 MB ≈ 1.5 GB — well inside Chrome's
717	  per-origin quota on a training laptop. Wins offline-first; matches the
718	  rest of the local-first storage idiom.
719	- Tagging UX is **one cue per clip, one tag, scrub-bar + frame step**.
720	  Multi-tag is deferred. Single-tag is the smallest shape that satisfies
721	  the acceptance criteria and keeps the engine path clean.
722	- The scheduler is **bypassed for clip mode**; the clip element itself
723	  is the "pre-cue delay" generator. A thin `clipRunner` slice owns the
724	  per-rep state machine and calls into the same `recordPress` path the
725	  keyboard/pedal/phone listeners use today.
726	- Decompose into **3 sub-phases**: 6.1 import+store, 6.2 tag, 6.3 play+record.
727	
728	### 1. Storage strategy — Blob in Dexie (Option A)
729	
730	| Option | Persistent | Cross-reload | Quota ceiling | Notes |
731	|---|---|---|---|---|
732	| (a) Blob in Dexie | yes | yes | ~10 % of disk (Chrome) | Fits idiom; one schema bump |
733	| (b) `URL.createObjectURL` ephemeral | no | no | RAM-bound | Clips re-imported every session — unusable |
734	| (c) File System Access API | yes | yes | full disk | Chrome-only, re-permission per session, breaks Phase-2b Android compat story |
735	
736	Recommend **(a)**. Add a new Dexie table `clips: 'id, importedAt'`
737	holding `{ id, name, mimeType, durationMs, sizeBytes, importedAt, blob }`.
738	Bump `db.ts` to `version(4)`. Playback resolves the blob via
739	`URL.createObjectURL(clip.blob)` at render time and `revokeObjectURL` on
740	unmount — same pattern Chrome uses for IndexedDB-backed media.
741	
742	Mitigation for quota exhaustion: surface `navigator.storage.estimate()`
743	in the clip-library screen, warn at >80 % usage, hard-cap at >95 % with
744	"delete a clip first". No silent failures.
745	
746	### 2. Tagging UX — one tag per clip, scrub + step
747	
748	Shape:
749	- Clip detail screen shows a `<video controls>` element plus a custom
750	  scrub bar with two buttons: **−1 frame** and **+1 frame** (step by
751	  `1/30s` since we don't know the source FPS; "good enough" for tagging
752	  at human reaction-time resolution).
753	- Athlete picks a `CueId` from the existing `CUE_LIBRARY` via a select
754	  (reuses the Phase-3 palette directly — no new cue data).
755	- Single tag persisted as `clip.cueId: CueId` + `clip.cueAtMs: number`.
756	- Edit overwrites; no version history.
757	
758	Multi-tag is explicitly deferred. Two tags on one clip means clip mode
759	also has to model "pre-cue delay between tag-1 finish and tag-2", which
760	re-introduces the scheduler we just bypassed. Not worth it for Phase 6.
761	
762	### 3. Playback engine integration — bypass the scheduler
763	
764	The Phase-5 engine assumes:
765	1. `pickPreCueDelayMs(rng, config)` → setTimeout → `revealCue()`
766	2. `CueStage` renders the cue
767	3. `recordPress(at)` classifies
768	
769	In clip mode steps 1 and 2 are *intrinsic to the video element*. The
770	clip plays from `t=0`; when `video.currentTime * 1000 >= clip.cueAtMs`,
771	that **is** "cue shown". The scheduler can't help — the timing source
772	is the video, not `setTimeout`.
773	
774	Recommend a **parallel runner** in `app/src/clipmode/runner.ts` (new
775	Zustand slice `useClipRunner`) that:
776	- picks a random clip from the enabled library (`pickRandomClip(rng, clips)`),
777	- mounts `<video>`, calls `play()` to capture `clipStartedAt =
778	  performance.now()`,
779	- on `timeupdate` (or `requestVideoFrameCallback` if available), when
780	  `video.currentTime * 1000 >= clip.cueAtMs`, fires
781	  `revealClipCue()` which records `cueShownAt = clipStartedAt + clip.cueAtMs`,
782	- routes presses through `recordPress(at)` *unchanged*.
783	
784	`useSession` is **not** reused for clip mode — clip runner produces its
785	own `RepRecord`s and `SessionRecord` directly via the existing `saveRep`
786	/ `saveSession` helpers. This keeps the Phase-5 scheduler untouched
787	(zero regression risk to shipped functionality) at the cost of some
788	duplication in the rep-commit code path (acceptable: ~30 lines).
789	
790	### 4. RT measurement — reuses recordPress without engine change
791	
792	`recordPress(at)` already takes a wall-clock `performance.now()` value
793	and diffs it against `cueShownAt`. As long as the clip runner produces
794	`cueShownAt = clipStartedAt + clip.cueAtMs` on the same `performance.now()`
795	clock, `classifyRep()` works as-is.
796	
797	**No engine change required.** `classifyRep()` is a pure function in
798	`engine/drill.ts` and accepts arbitrary `cueShownAt` / `pressedAt`
799	pairs. Reuse directly from the clip runner.
800	
801	One precision note: HTML5 `<video>` `timeupdate` fires at ~250 ms
802	resolution. Using `requestVideoFrameCallback` (Chrome 83+, Safari 15.4+)
803	brings this to per-frame (~16 ms at 60 fps), which matters because RT
804	measurement at <50 ms resolution is meaningless otherwise. Acceptance
805	gate: cue-shown event lands within **±33 ms** of the tagged frame.
806	
807	### 5. Results storage — additive `clipId` on RepRecord, additive `mode` on SessionRecord
808	
809	Smallest schema change:
810	- `RepRecord` gains `clipId?: string`.
811	- `SessionRecord` gains `mode?: 'live' | 'clip'` (default `'live'`,
812	  undefined treated as `'live'` for back-compat).
813	- Cue type is already on `RepRecord.cueId` — no change. The "results
814	  stored by clip and cue type" criterion is met by querying
815	  `reps.where('clipId').equals(id)` and grouping by `cueId`.
816	
817	No new `ClipSessionRecord` type. Reasoning: every Phase-5 analytics
818	function (`cueBreakdown`, `antiRhythmSignal`, `best10AvgOf`) operates
819	on `RepRecord[]`. A separate type would fork analytics. The two extra
820	optional fields cost nothing for live sessions and unlock per-clip
821	drilldown for free.
822	
823	Dexie change: bump to `version(4)`, add `clips: 'id, importedAt'`,
824	add `clipId` to the `reps` index → `reps: 'id, sessionId, cueId, clipId'`.
825	
826	### 6. Sub-phase decomposition (N=3)
827	
828	**Phase 6.1 — Clip library: import, store, list, delete**
829	- New `app/src/clipmode/library.ts` (pure: Blob → metadata extraction
830	  via offscreen `<video>` for `durationMs`).
831	- New `clipmode/db.ts` slice or extend `store/db.ts` with
832	  `addClip(blob)`, `listClips()`, `deleteClip(id)`.
833	- Dexie bump to `version(4)`; new `clips` table with the schema above.
834	- New `app/src/ui/ClipLibraryScreen.tsx` accessible from `IdleScreen`
835	  via a "Manage clips" link.
836	- Acceptance:
837	  - User picks a local .mp4 via `<input type="file" accept="video/mp4">`,
838	    sees it in the list with name, duration, size.
839	  - Reload preserves the list.
840	  - Delete removes blob + metadata.
841	  - Quota estimate visible; warning at >80 %.
842	  - `clipmode/library.test.ts` covers metadata extraction with a
843	    synthesized blob.
844	  - `app/verify-phase6-1.mjs` documents manual import of three clips.
845	
846	**Phase 6.2 — Tagging UI**
847	- New `app/src/ui/ClipTagScreen.tsx`: video element, scrub bar,
848	  frame-step buttons, cue-type select sourced from `CUE_LIBRARY`,
849	  Save button.
850	- Persists `cueId` + `cueAtMs` on the existing clip record (Dexie
851	  in-place update; no new version bump needed since the columns are
852	  blob-internal JSON, not indexed).
853	- Acceptance:
854	  - From clip library, "Tag" opens the tag screen prefilled if a
855	    prior tag exists.
856	  - Scrub + frame-step land within 1 frame of the chosen position.
857	  - Cue-type select shows all 8 entries from `CUE_LIBRARY`.
858	  - Save persists; reload preserves.
859	  - Untagged clips are flagged in the library list ("needs tag") and
860	    excluded from playback in 6.3.
861	  - `ClipTagScreen.test.tsx` covers cue-id selection + persistence.
862	
863	**Phase 6.3 — Random playback + RT measurement + per-clip results**
864	- New `app/src/clipmode/runner.ts` (Zustand slice).
865	- New `app/src/ui/ClipDrillScreen.tsx` (mounts `<video>`, drives the
866	  runner, renders the same `feedback` UI as `TrainerScreen`).
867	- `IdleScreen` gains a "Clip mode" start button that requires ≥1
868	  tagged clip.
869	- `RepRecord` gets `clipId?`, `SessionRecord` gets `mode?: 'clip' | 'live'`.
870	- Random selection via existing `rng.ts`; weighted-by-untaped-recently
871	  is *out of scope*.
872	- `SummaryScreen` shows a per-clip breakdown when `mode === 'clip'`,
873	  using `cueBreakdown(reps)` filtered by `clipId`.
874	- Acceptance:
875	  - Start "Clip mode" with 3 tagged clips → drill plays clips in
876	    random order.
877	  - Cue-shown event lands within ±33 ms of tagged frame (verified by
878	    `requestVideoFrameCallback` callback timestamp vs.
879	    `clipStartedAt + cueAtMs`).
880	  - Pressing keyboard/pedal/phone before cue → false start.
881	  - Pressing within hesitation threshold → correct_go with RT.
882	  - Pressing after late threshold → late.
883	  - Saved `SessionRecord.mode === 'clip'`; each `RepRecord` has the
884	    correct `clipId`.
885	  - Summary view groups results by clip → cue type.
886	  - `clipmode/runner.test.ts` exercises the state machine with a
887	    stubbed video element (manual `currentTime` advance).
888	  - `app/verify-phase6-3.mjs` documents a full library → tag → drill →
889	    summary flow.
890	
891	Each sub-phase is independently demoable: 6.1 ships a working clip
892	library (browse + delete); 6.2 makes clips tag-able and visible; 6.3
893	turns the system into a working video opponent.
894	
895	### 7. Risks / red-flags worth raising to architecture-red-team
896	
897	- **R1 — Blob quota assumption.** Chrome's per-origin quota is
898	  documented as "up to ~60 % of free disk" on desktop, but on
899	  constrained training laptops (older Chromebooks, MacBook Airs with
900	  small SSDs) athletes will hit ceilings. Red-team: is the >80 %
901	  warning + >95 % hard cap enough? Alternative: pre-import transcode
902	  via WebCodecs to reduce file size. Probably yes, but worth a second
903	  look.
904	- **R2 — `requestVideoFrameCallback` browser support.** Safari 15.4
905	  shipped it; Safari < 15.4 falls back to 250 ms `timeupdate`
906	  resolution which makes RT measurement unreliable. Two paths:
907	  (a) document Chrome/Edge/recent-Safari requirement and refuse to
908	  enable Clip mode otherwise, (b) ship anyway with degraded precision.
909	  No clear winner — depends on the athlete's actual training laptop.
910	- **R3 — Forked rep-commit path.** Bypassing `useSession` for clip
911	  mode means two pieces of code call `saveRep`/`saveSession`. Could

## Phase 6 decomposition memo — Video Opponent Mode

### Decision summary
- Clip mode is a **separate input/render path** that reuses the existing
  `recordPress(at)` boundary and `RepRecord` schema with one additive
  field. No engine surgery.
- Clips are stored as **Blob in Dexie** (Option A). Largest realistic
  Phase-6 library is ~30 clips × 50 MB ≈ 1.5 GB — well inside Chrome's
  per-origin quota on a training laptop. Wins offline-first; matches the
  rest of the local-first storage idiom.
- Tagging UX is **one cue per clip, one tag, scrub-bar + frame step**.
  Multi-tag is deferred. Single-tag is the smallest shape that satisfies
  the acceptance criteria and keeps the engine path clean.
- The scheduler is **bypassed for clip mode**; the clip element itself
  is the "pre-cue delay" generator. A thin `clipRunner` slice owns the
  per-rep state machine and calls into the same `recordPress` path the
  keyboard/pedal/phone listeners use today.
- Decompose into **3 sub-phases**: 6.1 import+store, 6.2 tag, 6.3 play+record.

### 1. Storage strategy — Blob in Dexie (Option A)

| Option | Persistent | Cross-reload | Quota ceiling | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Blob in Dexie | yes | yes | ~10 % of disk (Chrome) | Fits idiom; one schema bump |
| (b) `URL.createObjectURL` ephemeral | no | no | RAM-bound | Clips re-imported every session — unusable |
| (c) File System Access API | yes | yes | full disk | Chrome-only, re-permission per session, breaks Phase-2b Android compat story |

Recommend **(a)**. Add a new Dexie table `clips: 'id, importedAt'`
holding `{ id, name, mimeType, durationMs, sizeBytes, importedAt, blob }`.
Bump `db.ts` to `version(4)`. Playback resolves the blob via
`URL.createObjectURL(clip.blob)` at render time and `revokeObjectURL` on
unmount — same pattern Chrome uses for IndexedDB-backed media.

Mitigation for quota exhaustion: surface `navigator.storage.estimate()`
in the clip-library screen, warn at >80 % usage, hard-cap at >95 % with
"delete a clip first". No silent failures.

### 2. Tagging UX — one tag per clip, scrub + step

Shape:
- Clip detail screen shows a `<video controls>` element plus a custom
  scrub bar with two buttons: **−1 frame** and **+1 frame** (step by
  `1/30s` since we don't know the source FPS; "good enough" for tagging
  at human reaction-time resolution).
- Athlete picks a `CueId` from the existing `CUE_LIBRARY` via a select
  (reuses the Phase-3 palette directly — no new cue data).
- Single tag persisted as `clip.cueId: CueId` + `clip.cueAtMs: number`.
- Edit overwrites; no version history.

Multi-tag is explicitly deferred. Two tags on one clip means clip mode
also has to model "pre-cue delay between tag-1 finish and tag-2", which
re-introduces the scheduler we just bypassed. Not worth it for Phase 6.

### 3. Playback engine integration — bypass the scheduler

The Phase-5 engine assumes:
1. `pickPreCueDelayMs(rng, config)` → setTimeout → `revealCue()`
2. `CueStage` renders the cue
3. `recordPress(at)` classifies

In clip mode steps 1 and 2 are *intrinsic to the video element*. The
clip plays from `t=0`; when `video.currentTime * 1000 >= clip.cueAtMs`,
that **is** "cue shown". The scheduler can't help — the timing source
is the video, not `setTimeout`.

Recommend a **parallel runner** in `app/src/clipmode/runner.ts` (new
Zustand slice `useClipRunner`) that:
- picks a random clip from the enabled library (`pickRandomClip(rng, clips)`),
- mounts `<video>`, calls `play()` to capture `clipStartedAt =
  performance.now()`,
- on `timeupdate` (or `requestVideoFrameCallback` if available), when
  `video.currentTime * 1000 >= clip.cueAtMs`, fires
  `revealClipCue()` which records `cueShownAt = clipStartedAt + clip.cueAtMs`,
- routes presses through `recordPress(at)` *unchanged*.

`useSession` is **not** reused for clip mode — clip runner produces its
own `RepRecord`s and `SessionRecord` directly via the existing `saveRep`
/ `saveSession` helpers. This keeps the Phase-5 scheduler untouched
(zero regression risk to shipped functionality) at the cost of some
duplication in the rep-commit code path (acceptable: ~30 lines).

### 4. RT measurement — reuses recordPress without engine change

`recordPress(at)` already takes a wall-clock `performance.now()` value
and diffs it against `cueShownAt`. As long as the clip runner produces
`cueShownAt = clipStartedAt + clip.cueAtMs` on the same `performance.now()`
clock, `classifyRep()` works as-is.

**No engine change required.** `classifyRep()` is a pure function in
`engine/drill.ts` and accepts arbitrary `cueShownAt` / `pressedAt`
pairs. Reuse directly from the clip runner.

One precision note: HTML5 `<video>` `timeupdate` fires at ~250 ms
resolution. Using `requestVideoFrameCallback` (Chrome 83+, Safari 15.4+)
brings this to per-frame (~16 ms at 60 fps), which matters because RT
measurement at <50 ms resolution is meaningless otherwise. Acceptance
gate: cue-shown event lands within **±33 ms** of the tagged frame.

### 5. Results storage — additive `clipId` on RepRecord, additive `mode` on SessionRecord

Smallest schema change:
- `RepRecord` gains `clipId?: string`.
- `SessionRecord` gains `mode?: 'live' | 'clip'` (default `'live'`,
  undefined treated as `'live'` for back-compat).
- Cue type is already on `RepRecord.cueId` — no change. The "results
  stored by clip and cue type" criterion is met by querying
  `reps.where('clipId').equals(id)` and grouping by `cueId`.

No new `ClipSessionRecord` type. Reasoning: every Phase-5 analytics
function (`cueBreakdown`, `antiRhythmSignal`, `best10AvgOf`) operates
on `RepRecord[]`. A separate type would fork analytics. The two extra
optional fields cost nothing for live sessions and unlock per-clip
drilldown for free.

Dexie change: bump to `version(4)`, add `clips: 'id, importedAt'`,
add `clipId` to the `reps` index → `reps: 'id, sessionId, cueId, clipId'`.

### 6. Sub-phase decomposition (N=3)

**Phase 6.1 — Clip library: import, store, list, delete**
- New `app/src/clipmode/library.ts` (pure: Blob → metadata extraction
  via offscreen `<video>` for `durationMs`).
- New `clipmode/db.ts` slice or extend `store/db.ts` with
  `addClip(blob)`, `listClips()`, `deleteClip(id)`.
- Dexie bump to `version(4)`; new `clips` table with the schema above.
- New `app/src/ui/ClipLibraryScreen.tsx` accessible from `IdleScreen`
  via a "Manage clips" link.
- Acceptance:
  - User picks a local .mp4 via `<input type="file" accept="video/mp4">`,
    sees it in the list with name, duration, size.
  - Reload preserves the list.
  - Delete removes blob + metadata.
  - Quota estimate visible; warning at >80 %.
  - `clipmode/library.test.ts` covers metadata extraction with a
    synthesized blob.
  - `app/verify-phase6-1.mjs` documents manual import of three clips.

**Phase 6.2 — Tagging UI**
- New `app/src/ui/ClipTagScreen.tsx`: video element, scrub bar,
  frame-step buttons, cue-type select sourced from `CUE_LIBRARY`,
  Save button.
- Persists `cueId` + `cueAtMs` on the existing clip record (Dexie
  in-place update; no new version bump needed since the columns are
  blob-internal JSON, not indexed).
- Acceptance:
  - From clip library, "Tag" opens the tag screen prefilled if a
    prior tag exists.
  - Scrub + frame-step land within 1 frame of the chosen position.
  - Cue-type select shows all 8 entries from `CUE_LIBRARY`.
  - Save persists; reload preserves.
  - Untagged clips are flagged in the library list ("needs tag") and
    excluded from playback in 6.3.
  - `ClipTagScreen.test.tsx` covers cue-id selection + persistence.

**Phase 6.3 — Random playback + RT measurement + per-clip results**
- New `app/src/clipmode/runner.ts` (Zustand slice).
- New `app/src/ui/ClipDrillScreen.tsx` (mounts `<video>`, drives the
  runner, renders the same `feedback` UI as `TrainerScreen`).
- `IdleScreen` gains a "Clip mode" start button that requires ≥1
  tagged clip.
- `RepRecord` gets `clipId?`, `SessionRecord` gets `mode?: 'clip' | 'live'`.
- Random selection via existing `rng.ts`; weighted-by-untaped-recently
  is *out of scope*.
- `SummaryScreen` shows a per-clip breakdown when `mode === 'clip'`,
  using `cueBreakdown(reps)` filtered by `clipId`.
- Acceptance:
  - Start "Clip mode" with 3 tagged clips → drill plays clips in
    random order.
  - Cue-shown event lands within ±33 ms of tagged frame (verified by
    `requestVideoFrameCallback` callback timestamp vs.
    `clipStartedAt + cueAtMs`).
  - Pressing keyboard/pedal/phone before cue → false start.
  - Pressing within hesitation threshold → correct_go with RT.
  - Pressing after late threshold → late.
  - Saved `SessionRecord.mode === 'clip'`; each `RepRecord` has the
    correct `clipId`.
  - Summary view groups results by clip → cue type.
  - `clipmode/runner.test.ts` exercises the state machine with a
    stubbed video element (manual `currentTime` advance).
  - `app/verify-phase6-3.mjs` documents a full library → tag → drill →
    summary flow.

Each sub-phase is independently demoable: 6.1 ships a working clip
library (browse + delete); 6.2 makes clips tag-able and visible; 6.3
turns the system into a working video opponent.

### 7. Risks / red-flags worth raising to architecture-red-team

- **R1 — Blob quota assumption.** Chrome's per-origin quota is
  documented as "up to ~60 % of free disk" on desktop, but on
  constrained training laptops (older Chromebooks, MacBook Airs with
  small SSDs) athletes will hit ceilings. Red-team: is the >80 %
  warning + >95 % hard cap enough? Alternative: pre-import transcode
  via WebCodecs to reduce file size. Probably yes, but worth a second
  look.
- **R2 — `requestVideoFrameCallback` browser support.** Safari 15.4
  shipped it; Safari < 15.4 falls back to 250 ms `timeupdate`
  resolution which makes RT measurement unreliable. Two paths:
  (a) document Chrome/Edge/recent-Safari requirement and refuse to
  enable Clip mode otherwise, (b) ship anyway with degraded precision.
  No clear winner — depends on the athlete's actual training laptop.
- **R3 — Forked rep-commit path.** Bypassing `useSession` for clip
  mode means two pieces of code call `saveRep`/`saveSession`. Could
  drift. Mitigation considered: extract a `commitRep()` helper to a
  new `engine/persistence.ts` that both `session.ts` and `runner.ts`
  call. Decided **against** for Phase 6.1–6.3 to keep the diff small;
  red-team should sanity-check that the duplication risk is bounded
  (~30 lines, both call sites in the same repo).
- **R4 — Tag granularity.** Single-tag-per-clip means "opponent steps
  in, then blitzes" must be two separate clips. Athletes may want
  multi-tag for realism. Confirm with the spec author that single-tag
  is acceptable for the post-tournament window, or queue a Phase 6.4
  for multi-tag (would need a `tags[]` schema + a synthetic-delay
  generator between tags).
- **R5 — Frame-step precision.** Hard-coded 1/30s step assumes a 30 fps
  source clip. A 60 fps phone-recorded clip would step by 2 frames at
  a time; a 24 fps cinema clip steps by 0.7 frames (likely no visible
  change). The fix is to extract FPS at import via
  `requestVideoFrameCallback` sampling, but that costs ~50 lines and
  may be unnecessary for the training use case. Red-team: tolerate
  hardcoded 30 fps step, or extract real FPS?
- **R6 — IdleScreen mode selector UX.** A second "Start" button on the
  IdleScreen is the cheapest path; a mode toggle / segmented control
  is cleaner. Bike-shed risk — flag for red-team to pick the shape so
  6.3 doesn't churn the UI shell twice.

### Red-team review — Phase 6 decomposition
